metadata.title: Long-term memory retention
metadata.description: A curated educational map separating synaptic plasticity, sleep-related consolidation, and motivation-mediated learning exposure.
metadata.educational_notice: Curated and educational, not comprehensive. Animal, human, associative, and experimental evidence remain visibly distinct.
example_questions: What mechanisms support long-term memory retention?
How could synaptic plasticity and sleep contribute to memory persistence?

context_defaults.population: general human research context, with explicitly labeled animal evidence
important_uncertainty: Encoding, consolidation, retrieval, attention, and motivation are distinct processes.
Several molecular links rely on non-human experimental evidence.

metadata.interpreted_summary: We interpreted this as a question about long-term memory consolidation and resistance to forgetting, while keeping attention, motivation, encoding, and retrieval distinct.

numerical_data.explanation: No approved numerical observations, identified unknown parameters, priors, likelihood, or identifiability review are included in this educational pack.

entities.name: Learning event
entities.description: An episode in which information is encountered and encoded; it is not itself equivalent to later retention.

entities.name: Patterned hippocampal synaptic activity
entities.description: Temporally structured activity in hippocampal circuits, represented here as a trigger for experimentally studied plasticity.

entities.name: NMDA-receptor signaling
entities.description: Glutamate-receptor signaling with context-dependent roles in induction of some forms of synaptic plasticity.

entities.name: Hippocampal long-term potentiation
entities.description: A persistent increase in synaptic efficacy after particular stimulation patterns; a laboratory plasticity phenomenon, not memory itself.

entities.name: Hippocampus-dependent spatial learning
entities.description: Acquisition of spatial information in tasks that depend on hippocampal function.

entities.name: Long-term memory persistence
entities.description: Maintenance of learned information across time, kept distinct from attention, motivation, encoding, and retrieval.

entities.name: Hippocampus
entities.description: A medial temporal-lobe structure involved in multiple forms and stages of memory.

entities.name: Dentate granule cell
entities.description: Principal neurons of the dentate gyrus examined in the foundational rabbit potentiation experiment.

entities.name: CA1 pyramidal neuron
entities.description: Hippocampal principal neurons targeted in a region- and cell-type-restricted mouse NMDAR knockout.

entities.name: Post-learning sleep episode
entities.description: A sleep period after learning; sleep contains multiple stages and physiological processes.

entities.name: NREM slow-oscillation activity
entities.description: Low-frequency cortical activity during non-rapid-eye-movement sleep, distinct from a stimulation device or protocol.

entities.name: Declarative-memory consolidation
entities.description: Post-encoding processes that stabilize declarative memories; no single measured signal represents the entire process.

entities.name: Slow-oscillatory transcranial stimulation
entities.description: An experimental noninvasive stimulation protocol studied during NREM sleep; not presented as a personal intervention.

entities.name: Striatal dopamine function
entities.description: Dopaminergic function in striatal regions, represented only at the level supported by the cited cognitive-effort study.

entities.name: Willingness to expend cognitive effort
entities.description: Choice to engage with more cognitively demanding tasks when benefits and costs vary.

entities.name: Learning engagement
entities.description: Sustained participation in a learning activity; represented as a proposed mediator, not a molecular memory mechanism.

entities.name: Effective learning exposure
entities.description: The amount and quality of actual contact with learning material.

entities.name: Experimental NMDA-receptor blockade
entities.description: A laboratory perturbation used to test receptor involvement; not an intervention for improving memory.

evidence.title: Long-lasting potentiation of synaptic transmission in the dentate area of the anaesthetized rabbit following stimulation of the perforant path

context.temporal_context: 30 minutes to approximately 10 hours after patterned stimulation

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Potentiated population responses were reported in 15 of 18 rabbits; no modern standardized effect estimate was supplied.
limitations: Animal physiology experiment with low direct human relevance.
Did not test behavior, naturalistic learning, NMDA receptors, or memory retention.
Population responses combine synaptic efficacy and neuronal excitability.
evidence.evidence_note: Repetitive patterned perforant-path stimulation was followed by durable potentiation of dentate population responses in most tested rabbits.

evidence.title: Selective impairment of learning and blockade of long-term potentiation by an N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor antagonist, AP5

population.description: Rats in controlled pharmacology, spatial-learning, and electrophysiology experiments

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Sample size and a standardized effect estimate were not available in the PubMed abstract used for curation.
limitations: Broad pharmacological blockade can affect processes other than plasticity.
The shared perturbation does not prove that LTP loss mediated the learning deficit.
Supports a rat spatial-learning paradigm, not every memory type or human retention.
evidence.evidence_note: AP5 blocked high-frequency-stimulation-induced hippocampal LTP and selectively impaired place learning while sparing a visual-discrimination task in the reported paradigm.

evidence.title: The essential role of hippocampal CA1 NMDA receptor-dependent synaptic plasticity in spatial memory

population.description: Adult mice with NMDAR1 deletion restricted to CA1 pyramidal neurons and controls

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Sample size and standardized effect estimate were not available in the PubMed abstract used for curation.
limitations: The deletion affects multiple NMDAR-dependent functions, not LTP alone.
Concerns mouse spatial acquisition rather than all memory, human retention, or resistance to forgetting.
evidence.evidence_note: CA1-restricted NMDAR1 deletion removed CA1 NMDA currents and LTP and impaired spatial memory while reported nonspatial learning remained intact.

evidence.title: Boosting slow oscillations during sleep potentiates memory

population.description: 13 healthy young adults in a controlled sleep-laboratory study

context.condition: 0.75-Hz transcranial stimulation during early nocturnal NREM sleep

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Small sample; exact standardized effect estimate is not encoded in this demo record.
limitations: Small single-laboratory sample.
Several sleep features changed, so one mediator was not isolated.
Does not establish benefit across populations, protocols, or memory types.
evidence.evidence_note: In this small controlled study, the 0.75-Hz condition increased slow oscillatory and spindle activity and improved retention of hippocampus-dependent declarative material relative to controls.

evidence.title: Slow oscillatory transcranial direct current stimulation (so-tDCS) during slow wave sleep has no effects on declarative memory in healthy young subjects

population.description: 23 analyzed healthy adults in a double-blind, placebo-controlled, counterbalanced crossover study

context.condition: 0.75-Hz bifrontal so-tDCS versus sham during NREM N2

evidence.uncertainty_measure: No significant stimulation effect was reported for declarative or procedural consolidation or measured sleep physiology.
limitations: Physiological target engagement was not demonstrated.
Protocol differences limit direct falsification of earlier findings.
evidence.evidence_note: This double-blind crossover study found no significant stimulation effect on declarative or procedural consolidation, sleep staging, spindle density, or EEG-band power.

evidence.title: Dopamine promotes cognitive effort by biasing the benefits versus costs of cognitive work

population.description: 50 healthy adults completing PET, pharmacology, gaze, and cognitive-effort choice procedures

context.condition: rewarded choices between different N-back loads

effect_estimate.measure: Spearman correlation between caudate dopamine synthesis capacity and cognitive-effort willingness on placebo

evidence.uncertainty_measure: Pharmacological effects depended on baseline synthesis capacity rather than showing an unconditional group-wide increase.
limitations: Did not measure learning exposure, encoding, consolidation, or retention.
PET synthesis capacity is observational.
Pharmacological manipulations were not dopamine-selective in every respect.
evidence.evidence_note: Greater caudate dopamine synthesis capacity was associated with willingness to select greater cognitive effort; pharmacological effects varied with baseline synthesis capacity.

assertions.subject: learning_event
assertions.interpretation: A learning event is represented as preceding neural activity, but the cited artificial-stimulation experiment did not study natural learning.
limitations: Model bridge rather than a directly tested edge in the cited study.

assertions.subject: patterned_synaptic_activity
assertions.interpretation: Particular activity patterns recruit NMDA-receptor-dependent signaling in the studied hippocampal plasticity paradigms.
limitations: Species, circuit, and stimulation-pattern specific.

assertions.subject: patterned_synaptic_activity
assertions.interpretation: Patterned perforant-path stimulation produced persistent potentiation of dentate population responses in rabbits.
limitations: Artificial stimulation and an electrophysiological endpoint, not behavioral memory.

assertions.subject: nmda_signaling
assertions.interpretation: NMDA-receptor function was required for the tested forms of hippocampal LTP induction under pharmacological and genetic perturbations.
limitations: Does not imply every form of plasticity depends on NMDA receptors.

assertions.subject: nmda_signaling
assertions.interpretation: Pharmacological blockade and CA1-restricted genetic deletion impaired specific spatial-learning outcomes.
limitations: Perturbations affect more than LTP and do not generalize to all memory forms.

assertions.subject: hippocampal_ltp
assertions.interpretation: LTP is a plausible mechanism component, but the cited perturbations do not identify LTP as the sole mediator of long-term memory persistence.
limitations: Missing direct mediation and human-retention evidence.

assertions.subject: sleep_episode
assertions.interpretation: NREM sleep includes slow-oscillatory activity; stimulation studies manipulate or attempt to manipulate this physiology.
limitations: Sleep contains many co-occurring processes.

assertions.subject: nrem_slow_oscillation
assertions.interpretation: A small stimulation study supports a contribution of slow-oscillation-related physiology to declarative consolidation, while a larger crossover study found no effect.
limitations: Mixed evidence and incomplete physiological target engagement.

assertions.subject: declarative_consolidation

context.temporal_context: retention across a post-learning sleep period

assertions.interpretation: Declarative consolidation is represented as contributing to later retention; the intervention evidence is protocol-specific and mixed.
limitations: Not a universal claim across memories or populations.

assertions.subject: slow_osc_stimulation
assertions.interpretation: One protocol changed measured slow oscillatory activity; another did not demonstrate target engagement or memory benefit.
limitations: Experimental device research, not a personal intervention recommendation.

assertions.subject: striatal_dopamine
assertions.interpretation: Caudate dopamine synthesis capacity was associated with willingness to choose greater cognitive effort on placebo.
limitations: Association does not establish a direct causal dopamine effect.

assertions.subject: cognitive_effort
assertions.interpretation: Willingness to expend effort may affect engagement, but the cited study used rewarded N-back choices rather than a retention task.
limitations: Downstream bridge was not measured in the cited study.

assertions.subject: learning_engagement
assertions.interpretation: Engagement is modeled as increasing effective exposure; this bridge is a conceptual assumption outside the cited experiment.
limitations: Requires direct educational or behavioral evidence not bundled in this pack.

assertions.subject: learning_exposure
assertions.interpretation: Effective exposure could indirectly affect what is retained, but retention was not measured in the cited dopamine-effort study.
limitations: Not established by the attached source; retained as an explicitly weak link.

assertions.subject: nmda_antagonism
assertions.interpretation: Experimental AP5 administration blocked NMDA-receptor-dependent processes in the rat paradigm.
limitations: Laboratory perturbation only; not a memory-improvement strategy.

hypotheses.title: Hippocampal NMDA-dependent plasticity
hypotheses.summary: Particular hippocampal activity patterns can recruit NMDA-receptor-dependent plasticity. Animal perturbation studies connect this machinery to selected spatial-learning outcomes, but no study here proves the full chain to general human memory persistence.
context_requirements: Memory type and task must be specified.
Species and hippocampal subregion must be preserved.
missing_links: Direct mediation from LTP to human long-term retention is not established by these records.
uncertainty: Pharmacological and genetic perturbations affect functions beyond LTP.
hypotheses.evidence_label: Strong animal mechanism; indirect for general human retention

hypotheses.title: Sleep-related declarative consolidation
hypotheses.summary: Slow-oscillation-related physiology during NREM sleep may contribute to declarative consolidation, but protocol-specific human stimulation results conflict.
context_requirements: Declarative rather than all memory outcomes.
missing_links: The causal contribution of the stimulated feature is not isolated from other sleep physiology.
uncertainty: A later double-blind crossover study reported a null result.

hypotheses.title: Motivation-mediated learning exposure
hypotheses.summary: Striatal dopamine-related variation may influence willingness to expend cognitive effort. Any path from that choice to later retention is indirect and remains unsupported in the bundled study.
context_requirements: Reward structure and task demands matter.
missing_links: Engagement, effective learning exposure, and retention were not measured by the cited study.
uncertainty: The supported first edge is partly observational.
This is not a direct synaptic-consolidation mechanism.
hypotheses.evidence_label: Human evidence for effort choice; downstream retention path unvalidated

interventions.name: Slow-oscillatory sleep stimulation (research object)
interventions.description: An experimental laboratory stimulation class studied during NREM sleep. Results in this pack are inconsistent, and the object is not presented for personal use.
major_safety_concerns: Requires research or clinical oversight; no self-administration guidance is provided.
unsupported_assumptions: Generalization to other populations, protocols, or memory types.

interventions.name: NMDA-receptor blockade (mechanistic perturbation)
interventions.description: A causal laboratory perturbation used to test pathway necessity in animals; it impairs rather than enhances the studied outcomes and is not a treatment proposal.
uncertainty: Broad perturbation affects more than the modeled transition.
major_safety_concerns: Not suitable for unsupervised human experimentation.
No dosing, route, or acquisition information is provided.
unsupported_assumptions: That inhibiting this pathway has any memory benefit.

interventions.name: Dopaminergic manipulation (research object)
interventions.description: Pharmacological manipulation used to probe cognitive-effort decisions. It did not test memory retention and is not presented as a memory intervention.
major_safety_concerns: Prescription and pharmacological risks require medical oversight.
unsupported_assumptions: That more cognitive effort necessarily improves learning or retention.

petri_model.name: Curated memory-plasticity systems model
petri_model.description: A deliberately simplified educational state-transition model linking a plasticity input to receptor signaling, intracellular signaling, plasticity-related products, and an accumulated consolidated-state output.

scenarios.label: Increase activation
scenarios.description: Increase the synthetic pathway input rate.

scenarios.label: Reduce input
scenarios.description: Reduce the synthetic pathway input rate.

assumptions: All states are dimensionless abstractions rather than measured concentrations.
Mass-action transitions are phenomenological and do not reproduce a complete biochemical pathway.
The synthetic parameters are for qualitative scenario comparison only.
Transcription and product states are model assumptions not directly established by the bundled evidence records.

places.name: Plasticity-related products
places.description: Abstract slowly produced factors supporting persistence.

places.name: Consolidated-state output
places.description: Accumulated model output, not a measured memory score.

places.name: Positive feedback state
places.description: Bounded abstract feedback supporting receptor-pathway persistence.

transitions.name: Plasticity input
assumptions: Synthetic constant drive approximates repeated input.

transitions.name: Receptor-dependent signaling
transitions.biological_event: Plasticity signal is converted into receptor activation.
assumptions: One aggregate transition replaces multiple molecular events.

transitions.name: Intracellular propagation
transitions.biological_event: Receptor activation drives an aggregate intracellular state.
assumptions: Phenomenological transition; molecular identity is intentionally unspecified.

transitions.name: Plasticity-product formation
transitions.biological_event: Intracellular signaling produces a slower plasticity-support state.
assumptions: Synthetic model bridge, not directly measured in the cited study.

transitions.name: Consolidated-output accumulation
transitions.biological_event: Plasticity-related products add to an output state.
assumptions: Output is not behavioral memory and has arbitrary units.

transitions.name: Feedback formation
transitions.biological_event: Product state produces a bounded feedback state.

transitions.name: Feedback reinforcement
transitions.biological_event: The abstract feedback state reinforces receptor-pathway activation.
assumptions: Exploratory positive-feedback loop, not identified from the source.
